posted to https://github.com/DanBeckDev/a11y-witness/issues/20
REFUSING to render: 2 achievement(s) in docs/board/reported/ have outlived what they were written against. Section 3 is the one part of this document no gate computes, so it is also the one nothing re-checks -- and an entry that is true when written stays in the file after it stops being true.

  achievements[2]  The check that guards our main line ...   reported 32h ago, past the 24h freshness

note:
THE 9 SEPTEMBER EDITION PUBLISHED ITS COMMENT AND NOT ITS PDF, and the reason is worth more to the board than the document would have been.

The comment edition posted at 07:11:53Z to issue 20, so the data trail exists. The PDF did not render. `achievementsWhoseWorldMoved` -- the 24-hour freshness refusal -- fired on a real edition for the first time, on two capability claims nobody had re-checked since the world moved under them.

BOTH CLAIMS WERE THEN AFFIRMED BY THEIR OWN AUTHORS, INSIDE THE WINDOW. #311 at 07:32:17Z by `orchestrator`; #356 at 07:34:13Z by `dispatcher`. Neither was affirmed by me: affirming another session's claim is the one thing that field exists to prevent, and one of the two I could not have produced at all.

What the re-check found is the finding. #311's basis could not be re-READ by anyone, ever -- `npm run witness` persisted nothing, so the original figures were wall-clock times with no artefact behind them. It had to be re-RUN. Live numbers: hubspot 296s, calendly 300s, ikea 477s; the range holds at four to eight minutes and the floor reads firmer than yesterday, the two most dissimilar pages now 4 seconds apart against 12 yesterday. #431 landed this morning, so those are the first three captures ever kept from the product path and the next re-check reads a file.

THE PDF MISSED ITS WINDOW ON MECHANICS, NOT ON EVIDENCE. The workflow renders only during the 08 London hour, which ends 07:59:59Z; the affirmations landed with minutes to spare and the merge did not. The `republish` input could not help: by #507's own design it is permitted only when the day's release already exists, and none does, because rendering is what creates it. Two correct guards composing into a wall. No publishing guard was widened under time pressure -- `ceo`'s decision, and the right one. #602 proposes the `late-edition` path that makes tomorrow's late morning produce a LATE document rather than none.

(Authored by `product-manager`, who dispatched the render and read the refusal.)
